facts.text: Jesterville grew from a post village founded in 1867 after Wicomico County split from Somerset and Worcester counties.
The Beaudley house, built around 1795, showcases Federal‑style architecture and is listed on the National Register for its agrarian history.
Westside Historical Society, formed in 1985, preserves the western Wicomico County heritage and hosts a family history library on Main Street.
In 2006 the society earned the Heritage Award from the Lower Eastern Shore Heritage Council for outstanding preservation work.
Rural electrification reached Jesterville in the 1930s through the Choptank Electric Cooperative, a New Deal project started in 1938.
Jesterville sits just 10 feet above sea level at 38°17′12″N 75°53′45″W, within the Salisbury, Maryland‑Delaware Metropolitan Statistical Area.
